pr_title: Fix ruleset shaders not being able to reference framework parts
pr_body:
Depends on:
- [ ] https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/pull/5739
- [ ] Framework bump

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/23116

Additional perk: ruleset-specific shaders are being cached in the game's `ShaderManager`, which fixes their recompilation on each gameplay enter.

issue_context.title: `RulesetShaderManager` fails to retrieve shaders bundled with the ruleset
issue_context.body:
### Type

Other

### Bug description

Most likely introduced with https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/23034.
Easiest way to recreate: in `TestSceneRulesetDependencies` in `TestRetrieveShader` change `LoadRaw` strings to a single `Dependencies.Get<ShaderManager>().Load("TestVertex", "TestFragment");` - it will fail, but as far as my understanding goes - it should not.

Ruleset example: https://github.com/EVAST9919/lazer-swing
Drawable in question: https://github.com/EVAST9919/lazer-swing/blob/master/osu.Game.Rulesets.Swing/Objects/Drawables/Pieces/PathSliderBody.cs

### Screenshots or videos

_No response_

### Version

master

### Logs

[runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/11138778/runtime.log)
comments: Are you able to check why it fails? Should be pretty quick if you have things setup.

Looks like the issue here is in  `ShaderManager.createShaderPart()`. It's calling to `renderer.CreateShaderPart` which internally trying to add `Internal` shaders from the provided manager. But since our manager is made with ruleset resources - there are none of them.
Potential solution would be overriding `LoadRaw` in `RulesetShaderManager` the same way as `Load`. (Which works as expected and adds back ability to mix framework vertex and custom fragment shaders, I've successfully tested both)

review_comments:
I'm not really fond of this approach, it feels more like a band-aid than a proper solution. Keeping the shader store alive after `DrawableRulesetDependencies` is disposed sounds pretty bad when it's the one who added the store in the first place.

This should be done at a high level during game startup (e.g. `OsuGame`/`OsuGameBase`), but either way making ruleset shaders available in non-gameplay scenes sounds bad generally. 

I would prefer something along the lines of a `RulesetShaderCache` that creates and caches `ShaderManager`s for each ruleset throughout the game's lifetime and then have `DrawableRulesetDependencies` cache the ruleset's shader manager and add the main shader manager as a fallback store (with framework support for `AddStore(ShaderManager)`)
